qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Halliburton possesses significant North American basin logistics density, specialized completion chemistry, and high operational switching costs during active drilling and completion campaigns. However, it fails empirical proof of moat: 10-year median ROIC is ~8.6-9.1%, far below the 12% hurdle, with severe negative returns during downcycles (-23.7% in 2016, -1.7% in 2019, -12.4% in 2020). Primary erosion threats include rapid consolidation among E&P operators (Exxon/Pioneer, Chevron/Hess, Diamondback/Endeavor) creating monopsony buyer power, commoditization of pressure pumping equipment, and cyclical E&P capex cuts.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Cyclical oilfield services provider with 10-year median ROIC of ~8.6-9.1%, well below the 12% hurdle. Lacks cycle-durable pricing power as consolidated E&P operators hold strong monopsony bargaining power, driving severe margin and ROIC collapses during energy downturns.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year historical ROIC (2016-2025) demonstrates heavy cyclicality: -23.7% (2016), 5.1% (2017), 8.6% (2018), -1.7% (2019), -12.4% (2020), 8.6% (2021), 12.3% (2022), 17.2% (2023), 15.4% (2024), and ~9.1% (2025), yielding a 10-year median ROIC of ~8.6-9.1% (fails >=12% hurdle). Net income exhibits multi-billion dollar losses during downcycles (-$5.8B in 2016, -$1.1B in 2019, -$2.9B in 2020). Revenue split between Completion & Production (~55-60%) and Drilling & Evaluation (~40-45%) leaves the business highly exposed to North American fracturing capex cycles and buyer pricing pressure from consolidated mega-independents.
